question.leadin: Democrat Pat Schroeder described this man's presidency as "Teflon-coated" because "nothing sticks to him."
question.text: Name this president who somehow survived scandals like the Iran-Contra Affair during his two terms in office in the 1980s.
question.clue: In this man's first inaugural address, which was written by Ken Khachigian, he controversially stated that "government is not the solution to our problems; government is the problem."

swap.text: As Attorney General under his brother John, this man personally authorized some of the FBI's requests, including wiretapping phones to spy on Martin Luther King.
swap.answerHtml: Robert Francis Kennedy (accept RFK; accept Bobby Kennedy; prompt on “Kennedy” alone)
swap.clue: In televised hearings, this counsel for the Senate Labor Rackets Committee attempted to ruin Teamster union president Jimmy Hoffa.

question.text: During the term of this president, tensions were heightened when the Soviets shot down an American U2 spy plane. This former World War II general spearheaded the construction of the Interstate Highway system.
question.answerHtml: Dwight D. Eisenhower [or Dwight David Eisenhower or David Dwight Eisenhower or Ike Eisenhower]
question.clue: That project was organized by Allan Dulles, who was the brother of this president's Secretary of State, John Foster Dulles.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about incidents that almost sparked direct war between the USA and the USSR during the 1960s.
swap.text: This American pilot's U-2 was shot down during a surveillance mission, and he was seen as a traitor after he admitted to the Russians that the United States was spying on them.
swap.clue: American usage of UAV's began not long after this pilot was shot down from his U-2 spy plane while flying a reconnaissance mission over Soviet Union airspace in 1960.

question.leadin: This man called his own energy bill the "moral equivalent of war", which critics nicknamed MEOW.
question.text: Name this President, who blamed everything on the public's "crisis of spirit" in the Malaise speech. His failed Operation Eagle Claw led to the formation of the JSOC and the resignation of Cyrus Vance.
question.clue: After Love Canal was declared a federal emergency area, this man signed the Superfund Law.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about United States international diplomacy during the presidencies of Nixon and Ford.
swap.text: Most of the diplomatic stance of their presidencies was shaped by this National Security Advisor and Secretary of State under both presidents. He won the Nobel Peace Prize for the Paris Peace Accords alongside Le Duc Tho.
swap.clue: This man, who may have coordinated the assassination of Archbishop Makarios, coined the term "constructive ambiguity" to describe his policy toward China.

question.text: Richard Brenneke claimed that this organization initiated Palme's assassination through the Masonic lodge P2 as part of Operation Gladio. This organization used radio-based disinformation to stage a coup during Operation PBSuccess.
question.clue: The downfalls of Jacobo Arbenz and Mohammed Mossadegh were orchestrated by this organization, which operated an aircraft whose pilot refused to use a suicide pill after crashing near Yekaterinburg.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about industrial disasters on American turf.
swap.text: This planned community became the site of an environmental disaster when a school was constructed on a chemical dumping site, which was discovered following birth defects and partially inspired the Superfund program.
swap.clue: The EPA used money from its Superfund program to help citizens clean up this place near Niagara Falls. This neighborhood is where Hooker Chemicals buried 21,000 tons of chemical waste.

question.text: A private secretary to Supreme Court justice Louis Brandeis, this man was a target of Joseph McCarthy and said, "I will not turn my back on Alger Hiss." For 15 points, name this author of Present at the Creation, who helped create the Truman Doctrine as Secretary of State.
question.clue: He was an early supporter of dismissing Douglas MacArthur from command of UN forces in Korea.

swap.leadin: At the time of his rise to prominence, he was being investigated for taking bribes from Pepsi-Cola.
swap.text: Identify this Wisconsin senator who won election in 1946 after smearing a nearly fifty-year-old opponent for not enlisting in World War II.
swap.clue: Despite being attacked by a Democratic Truth Squad, he defeated Thomas Fairchild in 1952 to become a Senator.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Warren Commission.
question.text: A member of the Commission was this CIA director and brother of Dwight Eisenhower's Secretary of State. This pipe-smoking lawyer directed the CIA in overthrowing governments in Guatemala and Iran.
question.answerHtml: Allen Welsh Dulles [do not accept “John Foster Dulles”]
question.clue: The exchange that Weiner claims featured the titular phrase was supposed to have taken place between Eisenhower and this man, who served as Director of Central Intelligence from 1953 to 1961.

swap.text: In 1982, this series of successor agreements to SALT II began to be negotiated. One treaty under this banner cut total missiles to 1600 with no more than six thousand warheads, and a second negotiated by and Yeltsin cut that number in half.
swap.clue: This successor to the Strategic Arms Limitation Treaty(SALT) II was proposed by Reagan in 1982, but signed by George H. Bush and Mikhail Gorbachev in 1991. It reduced long range missiles to 1600 per side and nuclear warheads down to 6000 per side.

question.leadin: This agency was created by a 1970 executive order of Richard Nixon.
question.text: Name this federal agency responsible for monitoring air and water quality.
question.clue: In 1977, Paulette Barnes filed a suit after being fired from this government agency for refusing sexual advances from a superior. This agency was founded during the Nixon administration and set regulations for catalytic converters.

swap.text: This Arkansas-born 30 year Senate vet was the Chairman of the SFRC from 1959-1974. His 1971 hearings on the Vietnam War brought forth John Kerry's testimony on war crimes.
swap.clue: One program established by this senator used surpluses from the sale of war goods and funded dudes like Aaron Copland and Robert Nozick.

question.text: The Federal Aid Highway Act of 1956 was based not on Eisenhower's plan but on one put forward by this politician. His son of the same name popularized the term "information superhighway."
question.clue: Along with Kefauver and LBJ, this senator from Tennessee refused to sign the Southern Manifesto.

swap.text: After Tydings' defeat, most of the members of the Tydings Committee worked for a similar committee named for this Nevada Democrat, the namesake and sponsor of the 1950 Internal Security Act passed over Truman's veto.
swap.clue: This senator was an avid admirer of Francisco Franco and a strong opponent of communist expansion. In 2017, a movement surfaced to rename his namesake airport in Las Vegas after Harry Reid.

question.leadin: Answer the following about industrial disasters in American history.
question.text: According to the findings of the Kemeny Commission, surprisingly little cancer-causing iodine was released from the partial meltdown of this Pennsylvania nuclear reactor in 1979.
question.clue: The contemporaneous film The China Syndrome is credited with exacerbating fear about this incident.

swap.leadin: The captain of this ship, William McGonagle, received the Medal of Honor for saving the lives of many crewmembers aboard it.
swap.text: Name this ship bombed by Israeli aircraft in 1967, killing thirty-four people. Officially, the attack on this ship was deemed a case of mistaken identity, though it may have been to cover up the forthcoming invasion of the Golan Heights.
swap.clue: On the fourth day of the war, this American ship was attacked by Israeli aircraft while off the north coast of the Sinai Peninsula, killing thirty-four people. Israel claimed that it mistook this ship for an Egyptian transport ship.

question.text: A Congressman from Illinois throughout the 1960s and 1970s, this Rockefeller Republican said in a debate that he regretted voting for the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution. He then ran as an Independent, but despite the support of several prominent liberals and independents, he mustered just 6 million votes in the November election.
question.clue: After losing the Republican nomination, this man ran as an independent, campaigning for a gas tax hike. Support from Rockefeller Republicans and intellectuals netted him seven percent of the vote.

swap.leadin: It was co-chaired by Senator John Tower, who refused to sign his name to its final report.
swap.text: Name this 1975 committee, chaired by a namesake Idaho senator, that investigated American intelligence-gathering operations and revealed that the CIA maintained stocks of shellfish toxin.
